method: Questions were researched with an evidence-only retrieval tool over one corpus of open-access and public-domain texts (see corpus.json). Each excerpt was checked word for word against the corpus passage it cites when this file was written; corpus_chunk numbers that passage in the corpus snapshot of 2026-10-01.
questions: What distinguishes thick from thin evaluative concepts?
Can the descriptive content of a thick concept be separated from its evaluation?
Is evaluation part of the meaning of thick terms?

evidence.excerpt: Even if calling something selfish evaluates it as bad in some way or respect, not just any bad act can count as selfish; it must also involve the agent giving a certain degree of priority to herself over others.
So the application of thick terms and concepts seems somehow to involve both evaluation and non-evaluative description.
The designation “thick concept” for concepts that combine evaluation and non-evaluative description originates in Bernard Williams’s Ethics and the Limits of Philosophy (Williams 1985).
Williams seems to have drawn the label “thick” from the notion of “thick description” introduced by Gilbert Ryle and adapted to other purposes by the anthropologist Clifford Geertz.
practical concepts such as shrewd and imprudent, epistemic concepts such as open-minded and gullible, and aesthetic concepts such as banal and gracious
courageous only if it involves some risk to the agent
It doesn’t seem possible to state what thick terms and concepts semantically express
just how offensive a remark has to be to count as ‘rude’ might vary with context
take this to mean that there are no thick concepts, but only loaded words; see Blackburn 1992 and, on the general phenomenon, Stevenson 1938
using “thick” to refer to terms and concepts that characteristically involve both evaluation and non-evaluative description in some way or other
What one seems to be at most required to accept is that x is lewd in some non-evaluative sense.
such as using scare quotes or a certain tone of voice
Many people regard the thick terms chaste and lewd as objectionable
